name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields ease after the Budget but stay near 19-year highs
state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.29% at the 30 Oct close and the 30-year 5.72%, near multi-decade highs. Yields fell to their lowest since 22 Sep after Chancellor John Healey's first Budget met the fiscal rules. Markets reopen on 2 Nov ahead of the 5 Nov Bank of England decision.
for_you: Fixed-rate mortgage pricing tracks gilt yields, so new fixed deals remain expensive by recent standards.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
